## Biography

I am a Ph.D. student in the Department of Plant Pathology and Environmental Microbiology at The Pennsylvania State University. I work under the supervision of Dr. Ricardo I. Alcalá Briseño.

My research focuses on fungal virology, with particular emphasis on the discovery, diversity, and functional characterization of mycoviruses associated with fungi exhibiting different trophic lifestyles. I combine molecular biology, high-throughput sequencing, and bioinformatics approaches to investigate how viral infections influence fungal physiology, metabolism, and interactions with the plant-host and the environment.

Before joining Penn State, I obtained my M.Sc. in Plant Biotechnology at CINVESTAV-Irapuato, my project was the development of synthetic bacterial communities and transformation methods for _Bacillus_ species. I received my B.Sc. in Biotechnology Engineering from Universidad Politécnica de Pénjamo, Guanajuato, Mexico.

I enjoy science communication and developing educational content that makes science more accessible to students and the general public.

## Current Research

My current research investigates the diversity and biological interactions of mycoviruses associated with fungi representing different ecological lifestyles, including plant pathogens, saprotrophs, and ectomycorrhizal fungi.

Current projects include:

- Identification of novel mycoviruses using high-throughput sequencing.
- Construction and curation of comprehensive mycovirus databases.
- Bioinformatic analysis of fungal viromes.
- Comparative analyses of viral diversity among fungal lifestyles.
- Functional characterization of virus-induced changes in fungal metabolism.
- Investigation of host–virus interactions using molecular biology and transcriptomics.
